answer: Violet is one forged identity, zenith is the elapsed epochs of client-paid judged work it must earn, and the ledge is the register where identities are anchored. A row is seated only once independent branches have each judged its work, and each branch's judgment seats one row, so two violets claiming the same branch collide on the ledge. The quorum widens as rows fill the ledge, so the thousandth violet needs more branches and more epochs than the first: paid hours that cannot be split. It breaks if branches share judgments or hand out zenith freely.
